    • upsert

      public Update upsert(List<ConvertedSection> convertedSections, edu.ucsb.cs156.jobs.services.JobContext ctx, String quarterYYYYQ, String subjectArea, boolean fromJob) throws Exception
      Insert or update each section in the convertedSections collection.
      Parameters:
      fromJob - true when called from UpdateCourseDataJob, which fetches a complete (subjectArea, quarter) with level "A". Only then do we (a) record enrollment data points, so enrollment history gets one point per scheduled run rather than one per user search, and (b) save an Update record, which IsStaleService reads as "this subject/quarter is fully loaded". User searches pass false: the main page only ever sends a partial level (L, S, U or G), and GE searches span many subjects, so neither may mark a subject/quarter as loaded.
      Returns:
      the Update summarizing this run; saved to the updates collection only when fromJob
      Throws:
      Exception

    • upsertAsync

      @Async("jobsExecutor") public void upsertAsync(List<ConvertedSection> convertedSections, String quarterYYYYQ, String subjectArea)
      Fire-and-forget write-through for the live-API search endpoints. The caller returns immediately, so the user's search response is never delayed by Mongo writes.

      Runs on lib-jobs' "jobsExecutor" (@EnableAsync is also provided by lib-jobs). That pool has 2 threads, so this can overlap a job or another search; upsert() is synchronized so the find-then-save can't insert duplicate sections. Waiting on that lock is fine for a cache fill.

      Must be called from another bean: Spring applies @Async through a proxy, so a call from inside this class would run synchronously.

      Exceptions are caught and logged here because an exception thrown from an @Async void method has no caller to propagate to.
